transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO - Constellation), Priya (ML), Marcus (Infra), Aisha (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros, I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with Constellation. Ethan and Luis are our SEs who will help with benchmarks and perf.
[00:10] Jared: Hi all, Jared here. We're focused on getting a POC scoped that shows both cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, ML eng; we'll own the prompt set and eval criteria.
[00:24] Marcus: Marcus, infra, will validate VPC/KMS and networking constraints.
[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, cost model assumptions, timeline.
[00:40] Ethan: I'll start with how we typically model unit economics. Roughly we break down per-token compute cost, amortized GPU overhead, and then optimization knobs: batching distribution, KV/prefix cache hit rates, and quantization profile.
[00:56] Priya: Can you define per-token compute cost? We have variable sequence lengths; our data has a heavy tail — median ~150 tokens, p95 ~1200.
[01:10] Ethan: Yes, for variable sequences we model effective cost per generated token as: (GPU compute time per token * GPU cost per second) + amortized overhead. In practice, shorter median helps but the p95 affects provisioning. We'll show a model that outputs per-token at med/p95 and a blended rate.
[01:26] Luis: Also batching helps reduce per-token cost but may increase tail latency. So we need your latency SLOs to choose batch size policy.
[01:36] Aisha: Our SLO: 200ms p50, 600ms p95 for conversational assistant. Is that realistically achievable?
[01:44] Ethan: Depends on model size and quantization. With a 7B open model, FP16 on A100 or H100 can hit that at modest batch sizes. With 4-bit quant and optimized kernels we can reduce cost but might add a few ms of decode overhead; sometimes quantized kernels are faster.
[02:00] Marcus: Our infra runs mostly on GCP with T4s and some A100 reservations. For a POC we can spin up a temporary H100 cluster if needed but need budget approval.
[02:10] Maya: Budget was flagged earlier by Aisha in the RFP — roughly $10k/month target for conversational features. We need to show unit economics to see if that maps to target queries/day.
[02:22] Priya: Typical workload: 60k user messages/day, average 180 tokens in prompts and 40 tokens generated. But spikes up to 10x during certain windows.
[02:34] Ethan: Ok, we'll use that traffic profile. Key knobs: batching (max batch size, latency-first or cost-first policy), KV/prefix cache hit rate — if you have many repeated prompts caching helps a lot — and quantization profile (FP16 vs 4-bit).
[02:50] Jared: How do you model KV cache impact?
[02:56] Luis: We estimate cache hit rate from prompt reuse. For example, with 30% prefix cache hit, effective compute per-request can drop by ~20-30% because early layers are skipped or KV retrieval is cheap. But exact numbers need your prompt set.
[03:12] Priya: We'll share a sample 1k prompt set including templates and agent-state.
[03:20] Ethan: Perfect. For the POC benchmarks we'll run controlled tests: 1) baseline FP16 with batch sizes tuned for latency SLOs; 2) 4-bit quant profile prioritized for cost; 3) caching enabled scenarios. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:40] Aisha: When you say cost per 1k tokens, do you include infra amortization and idle capacity?
[03:46] Maya: Yes, our cost model spreadsheet includes amortized reserved capacity (if Dedicated) or on-demand hosted pricing, plus storage and bandwidth rough estimates. We'll send assumptions.
[03:56] Marcus: Networking — if we run in our VPC we need to confirm egress and that Redwood supports our KMS. Is that documented?
[04:04] Ethan: We support customer KMS integrations and VPC peering for Private deployments; we'll share the security whitepaper. For the POC we can run in Redwood Dedicated using a private tenant with customer-managed keys, assuming an NDA.
[04:18] Jared: Competitors: we evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic; cost is competitive but we need on-prem/VPC options and predictable cost for enterprise.
[04:28] Maya: Understood. The POC goal can be: demonstrate X qps at <=600ms p95 for 90% of traffic and show unit cost < $0.0025 per generated token (example target).
[04:42] Priya: That target per-token seems tight; can you show sensitivity to batching?
[04:46] Ethan: Absolutely. e.g., with batch size 8 and no cache, per-gen-token cost might be $0.0035 on on-demand; with batch size 32 where latency allows, cost can drop to $0.0018. With a 30% cache hit and quant 4-bit, we can reach your $0.0025 target in some mixes. We'll produce a table.
[05:06] Luis: We'll also measure throughput plateaus — important to understand tail queuing. We'll run simulated traffic with your 60k/day profile including 10x spikes.
[05:16] Marcus: For the benchmark env, we prefer Redwood spins up dedicated nodes in our GCP project, or snapshots of your Dedicated offering. We need the test to mimic egress limits and CPU/GPU types.
[05:28] Ethan: We can do two runs: Redwood-managed Dedicated instance in our environment and a containerized test you run in your infra. The latter helps validate network and KMS interactions.
[05:38] Jared: Timeline?
[05:40] Maya: Proposal: Maya sends cost model spreadsheet and POC plan by Monday (2026-03-16). Customer shares prompt set and traffic profile by Wednesday (2026-03-18). Redwood runs initial benchmarks by 2026-03-22 and we schedule follow-up on 2026-03-24 to review results. Does that work?
[05:56] Priya: Yes.
[05:58] Marcus: Works for infra.
[06:00] Aisha: Quick question on metrics — can you include token-level cost and per-request bill estimates for 10k/50k/100k daily users?
[06:08] Ethan: Yes, we'll produce scenarios in the spreadsheet. Also include a best-practice set of batching policies (adaptive batching), cache TTL recommendations, and quantization tradeoffs.
[06:18] Jared: Any risks to watch for?
[06:20] Luis: Main risks: quantization regression on quality, misestimated cache hit rates, and network egress causing latency spikes. We'll propose canary runs and A/B evals to catch regressions.
[06:34] Maya: Recap of next steps and action items — see chat.
[06:38] Jared: Thanks everyone, excited to see numbers.
[06:42] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with doc links and the spreadsheet.
[06:46] (call ends)
notes: References: Redwood cost model spreadsheet (link to be shared), security whitepaper and KMS integration docs. Customer to provide sample prompt set and traffic histogram. Agreed target: p95 <= 600ms, per-generated-token target ~ $0.0025 as a working goal.
references: Cost model spreadsheet (link will be shared by Maya)
